The reference labels keep only the verb and object of the same actions. The description states these actions with the extra phrase as a detail, so the label should keep the co)

same as LRN-061 (The records show the generated model omitted the Architect pool, the Online stores pool, and the four cross-pool message flows (send requirements to the architect, draft back to the draft-received catch event, place order to the stores, and the stores' return to the Get order catch event). The reference, the description, and BPMN 2.0.2 agree on this. The lane records (C2, C4, C5) are not supported)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description attaches a purpose, means, or recipient phrase to a described action (for example 'to ...', 'with additional ...', or 'to <party>' after the verb and object): Label the task with the main verb and object of the stated action only, and leave the purpose, means, or recipient phrase out of the label. Keep the wording close to the description's verb and object, so the label stays faithful and short.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description attaches a purpose, means, or recipient phrase to a described action (for example 'to ...', 'with additional ...', or 'to <party>' after the verb and object)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that an action performed by one participant sends a message to another participant, or that another participant's start or wait point depends on that action, whether the other participant is a peer in the process or an external party acting on its own: Model each participant as its own pool in one collaboration. Draw every cross-participant dependency as a message flow from the sending participant's task (or throw event) to a message start event or intermediate message catch event in the receiving participant's pool. Do not connect elements of different pools with sequence flows. Do not connect a sending task to a catch event inside the same pool with a message flow. Do not reverse the flow so that the receiving start or catch event is the source.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description has the process send a request or an order to a party outside the process, such as a service provider or a store, that acts on its own, and the process later continues only after that party returns a deliverable or confirmation

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description names work that the performer carries out by hand himself, such as receiving physical goods or building something from them, with no system or message exchange involved: Model such hands-on work as a manualTask in the performer's flow, placed at the point where the description performs it. Do not model the physical receipt or handling of goods as an intermediate catch event or as a generic task. Reserve intermediate catch events for waits on an external message, signal, time or condition.
rules_sent_back.situation: The description says that a party other than the performer carries out physical building or assembly work, and it describes no reply message, signal, time, or condition that the process waits for before continuing.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says a received result is refined several times with additional input, so the decision on whether another round is needed is implied but not stated as a question, and the loop back to the refinement is the only branch the generator modeled: Model an exclusive gateway after the result is received and before the loop back to the refinement task. Its outgoing branches are a judgment on whether the current result is sufficient (the loop back for further input, and the exit to the next step). Label the gateway as a question about the result's sufficiency or acceptability, using the description's own words for the result, not the name of the next action. Label the refinement task with the input the description gives it.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says a received result is refined several times with additional input, so the decision on whether another round is needed is implied but not stated as a question, and the loop back to the refinement is the only branch the generator modeled

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says a participant sends requirements, materials, or orders to several separate outside parties, and at least one of those parties returns something the participant later waits for or reacts to: Represent the participant and each separate outside party as its own bpmn:participant pool in one bpmn:collaboration, one pool per distinct party, including when several parties play the same role. Draw a message flow from each sending task to the pool of the party it addresses, and draw a message flow from each returning party to an intermediate message catch event in the participant's pool. Do not join these pools with sequence flows, and do not merge several distinct parties into one pool.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says a participant sends requirements, materials, or orders to several separate outside parties, and at least one of those parties returns something the participant later waits for or reacts to

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that the performer personally contacts several other people as an action of its own, with no system or software transmitting that contact and no reply the process waits for, and the generated model uses a sendTask for that contact: Model that hand-performed contacting as a manualTask in the performer's lane, placed where the description performs it. Reserve sendTask for a message that the description says is transmitted through a system or to a participant's interface. Do not add a waiting intermediate catch event after the contact unless the description says a reply or notice is awaited.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that the performer personally contacts several other people as an action of its own, with no system or software transmitting that contact and no reply the process waits for, and the generated model uses a sendTask for that contact

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the process sends an order or request to one or more outside parties, and while those parties process it the process goes on with other work that runs in parallel, so the delivery or reply is only needed at a later join point: Model each outside party that receives the order or request as a separate pool in the collaboration. Draw a message flow from the sending task to that pool. Place the wait for the delivery or reply as an intermediate message catch event in its own parallel branch, between the parallel split that starts the work and the parallel join that waits for it. Draw a message flow from the outside pool into that catch event. Do not connect the outside pool with sequence flows, and do not model the wait as a task or leave it out of the parallel branch.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says the process sends an order or request to one or more outside parties, and while those parties process it the process goes on with other work that runs in parallel, so the delivery or reply is only needed at a later join point
